💼 Company: Mercor
🌍 Work Mode: 100% Remote
💰 Compensation: $80 per hour
⏰ Engagement: Flexible Hourly Contract
🔥 Status: New Opportunity – Early Applicants Welcome!

Are you an experienced Mechanical Engineer passionate about product design, manufacturing, and advanced engineering technologies?

Mercor is seeking Senior Mechanical Engineering Professionals to help build real-world evaluation tasks for next-generation AI systems working in Fortune 500 engineering and manufacturing environments.

🔹 Key Responsibilities:
✅ Develop complex mechanical engineering scenarios.
✅ Create product design and CAD modeling tasks.
✅ Work on thermal, fluid, structural, and stress analysis scenarios.
✅ Develop manufacturing and reliability engineering assessments.
✅ Apply FEA, CFD, DFM/DFA, Six Sigma, and GD&T principles.
✅ Create engineering reference solutions and evaluation rubrics.
✅ Work with tools such as SolidWorks, ANSYS, CATIA, MATLAB/Simulink, and PLM systems.

✔️ 5+ years of Mechanical Engineering experience.
✔️ Experience in Fortune 500 or major industrial companies.
✔️ Strong knowledge of product design and manufacturing processes.
✔️ Familiarity with ASME or ISO engineering standards.
✔️ Experience in automotive, aerospace, industrial, or manufacturing sectors.
✔️ PE, CEng, or EUR ING credentials are an added advantage.

🌎 Standards Tracks:
🇺🇸 US Track – ASME
🌍 International Track – ISO
💳 Payment: Weekly payments through Stripe or Wise.

Senior Mechanical Engineers, Engineering Leads, Product Design Engineers, Manufacturing Engineers, Aerospace Engineers, and FEA/CFD Specialists.

Build the Infrastructure. Shape the Future. Own the Foundation.
Are you an infrastructure leader who loves building things from the ground up rather than managing legacy systems?
We're looking for a Senior Infrastructure Leader (10–12+ years) to architect and build the corporate IT, cloud, identity and security infrastructure for a fast-growing AI company.
This is a founding leadership opportunity where you'll be a hands-on builder, technology owner and strategic problem solver.
🔹 What You'll Own:
Build and scale corporate IT infrastructure, employee technology and endpoint management.
Lead cloud infrastructure across AWS / Azure / GCP.
Establish Identity & Access Management (SSO, MFA, RBAC, Okta / Entra).
Drive Infrastructure-as-Code using Terraform / OpenTofu.
Manage GitHub, developer tools, networking, secrets and cloud security.
Govern enterprise AI platforms – OpenAI, Claude, Gemini and Copilot.
Establish security frameworks, SOC 2 / ISO 27001 readiness and FinOps practices.
Build and lead the infrastructure team as the organisation scales.
🔹 What We're Looking For:
10–12+ years of experience across IT Infrastructure, Cloud and Infrastructure Operations.
Proven experience building infrastructure from scratch in a startup or fast-growing organisation.
Strong hands-on expertise in cloud platforms, automation, identity management and security.
Experience managing IT, cloud, SaaS vendors and infrastructure budgets.
A builder's mindset, ownership mentality and comfort operating in a fast-paced environment.
🌟 Why This Opportunity?
This isn't about maintaining an existing infrastructure setup. It's about creating the technology backbone of an AI-first organisation and shaping how it scales.

💼 Role: Full-time | 12-18 Months Contract | Senior Leadership
🎯 Experience: 10–12+ Years

Someone asked me.

What's the biggest red flag on a CV that gets candidates rejected?

My answer: Frequent short-term employment.

But context matters.

For contract roles:

Short tenures are normal.

Just make it clear that the roles were project-based, fixed-term or temporary.

For permanent roles:

It's a different story.

Imagine a CV showing:

Company A: 8 months
Company B: 10 months
Company C: 6 months
Company D: 9 months

The hiring manager immediately wonders:

"Will this person stay with us?"

Many employers prefer 3–5 years of stability.

But let's be realistic.

Layoffs, project cancellations, budget cuts and AI-driven restructuring have changed the job market.

Not every short tenure is your fault.

So how do you reduce the risk?

Explain short tenures on your CV.

Get LinkedIn recommendations from former managers and department heads.

Work with a recruiter who has a strong client relationship and can personally vouch for your skills.

Here's the reality:

Your short employment history isn't necessarily the problem. 

The lack of context is.
Your skills get you shortlisted.
Your credibility gets you hired.
Have you ever been rejected because of frequent job changes?

Your employees are already pasting CVs, appraisals and complaints into AI tools.

Is your organisation ready for what the DPDP Act says about that? - https://lnkd.in/dR2fiRnT

Recruiters summarising resumes. Managers drafting performance notes. Support teams analysing complaints. Often on personal accounts, with no one tracking it.

Under the DPDP Act, 2023, your organisation is the Data Fiduciary. Using an AI tool does not remove that responsibility.

📅 The date to mark: 13 May 2027

 That's when the main provisions kick in: notice, consent, fiduciary duties, individual rights and penalties. Phase 2 (13 Nov 2026) covers Consent Managers only, so the real deadline for employers is still ahead. 

That's your preparation window.

💰 What's at stake
 Penalties can reach ₹250 crore for failing to maintain reasonable security safeguards, and ₹200 crore for failing to notify a breach.

⚠️ Where the risk hides
Shadow AI on personal accounts
Resumes and appraisals pasted into public tools

AI summaries used as the sole basis for hiring or promotion decisions
Employees leaving with work chats in personal AI accounts

Deleting a prompt ≠ deleting the data (and it doesn't cancel reporting duties)

 1️⃣ Map your data and AI tools, including unapproved ones
 2️⃣ Document the lawful ground for each use
 3️⃣ Apply security safeguards: access controls, MFA, logging
 4️⃣ Review vendor contracts, retention and breach reporting
 5️⃣ Set up a breach response process
 6️⃣ Create a grievance and rights-request channel
 7️⃣ Train employees by role

The goal isn't to ban AI. It's to build clear guardrails so your teams can use it with confidence.

AI isn’t wiping out the IT industry overnight—but it is quietly erasing the bottom and middle rungs of the tech career ladder.
Over the past year, we’ve seen a clear shift. Companies aren't just cutting headcount to save money; they are reallocating budgets toward AI infrastructure and letting routine execution roles vanish.
Here is a realistic look at what AI is displacing right now, and where the wave is heading over the next 5 years (2026–2031).
What AI is taking right now:
 * Tier 1 & Tier 2 IT Support: AI agents already resolve roughly 80% of routine helpdesk tickets, password resets, and basic troubleshooting.
 * Junior & Contract Dev Roles: Boilerplate code, standard CRUD features, and routine bug fixes are increasingly generated in seconds, shrinking entry-level hiring.
 * Manual QA & Basic Ops: Repetitive regression testing, log monitoring, and standard infrastructure provisioning are being absorbed by automated pipelines.
What’s at risk in the next 5 years:
Displacement is moving up the value chain—straight into the "middle" of IT:
 * Mid-Level "Spec-to-Code" Developers: Engineers who primarily translate clear tickets into standard features or API integrations will face the steepest squeeze.
 * Basic Data Analysts & BI Report Builders: Writing boilerplate SQL, building routine dashboards, and drafting weekly KPI summaries are becoming single-prompt tasks.
 * Standard Front-End & Routine QA Automation: Page layouts, standard UI components, and basic automated test scripts are rapidly being handled by self-healing AI agents.
 * Traditional Maintenance & Staff Augmentation: Large billable-hour teams are losing ground to smaller, senior-heavy squads amplified by AI.
What remains resilient through 2031:
When AI can write 75%+ of routine code, the market stops paying a premium for syntax—and starts paying for judgment, architecture, and accountability.
The roles growing instead:
 * System & Solution Architects who can verify AI output, spot hidden technical debt, and own complex trade-offs.
 * Distributed Systems, Platform, and AI Infrastructure Engineers.
 * Cybersecurity, Adversarial Defense, and AI Governance specialists.
 * Incident Commanders and technical leaders who align technology with real business ROI.
The biggest risk over the next five years isn't AI itself—it's staying comfortable in a role built on routine execution.

According to the Calabria Administrative Court: the Cutro transition rules preserve conversion for certain special-protection permits

According to the Calabria Administrative Court: the Cutro transition rules preserve conversion for certain special-protection permits

Changes in Italian immigration legislation frequently raise an essential question: what happens to permits obtained before a restrictive reform? The Calabria Regional Administrative Court, Catanzaro, Second Section, dealt with this in judgment no. 460 of 7 March 2025, concerning the conversion of special-protection residence permits into work permits.

The legal dispute

Decree-Law 20/2023, subsequently converted by Law 50/2023, altered the ordinary framework for special protection and conversion. Its Article 7(3), however, preserved a transitional regime for qualifying permits already issued and still valid. The court examined whether that protection could also encompass permits issued by the Questore following a recommendation for special protection under Article 32 of Legislative Decree 25/2008.

What the court held

The Court's officially published summary explains that the transitional protection is not confined exclusively to a formal label referring to Article 19(1.1) of Legislative Decree 286/1998. A permit issued through the Article 32 procedure is substantively linked to the same protection requirements. For the qualifying already-issued permits, the possibility of conversion into a work residence permit therefore remains, provided the statutory employment requirements are met.

Practical implications

Applicants and lawyers should retrieve the original protection decision, the residence card, issue and expiry dates, previous renewals and proof of employment. A refusal invoking the Cutro reform generically should be compared with the actual transitional provision and the procedural origin of the permit. The employer's declaration, contract, mandatory hiring notice and other work-related requirements must still be reviewed.

The judgment does not create unconditional conversion rights for all special-protection permits issued at any time. It highlights the importance of establishing the original legal basis and temporal application of the statute. Where a final refusal is received, the appropriate remedy and deadline must be assessed individually; a successful challenge generally requires renewed lawful consideration, not automatic issuance.

Riferimento giudiziario / Judicial reference: TAR Calabria, Catanzaro, sezione II, 7 marzo 2025, n. 460. Fonte verificabile / Source.

The Bengaluru startup records people doing real work in factories, warehouses, farms and homes, then labels it as training data for robotics and physical AI models. Accel led the $26M equity. Lighthouse Canton led the $21M venture debt, with Trifecta Capital.

1. 12 paying customers, about 90% of revenue from the US.

3. The company says it crossed $50M in annualised revenue within six months of operations.

Structured LLM outputs are the difference between an AI demo and an AI feature.

When I built the Automated Expense Categorizer & Cashflow Forecaster for a small business finance app, the first version asked the model for free-text answers and then tried to parse them. It worked on my test data and fell apart on real bank CSVs.

The fix was to define a strict output schema up front and treat the model as a function that must return that shape. Every categorisation came back with a fixed set of fields, and anything that didn't validate got retried or flagged for review.

What I took from it as a full stack engineer:

→ Write the schema before the prompt
→ Validate model output on the server, not in the UI
→ Log every rejected response, because that's where your next prompt improvement lives
→ Keep the cashflow maths in plain Python so it stays testable

The stack was Python on the backend, React.js on the front, and PostgreSQL for storing categorised transactions.

For engineers building AI features across Australia: how are you enforcing output contracts from your LLMs today? Hiring managers, I'd also like to hear what you look for when reviewing AI work in a candidate's portfolio.

We're hiring experts, not annotators. 🔴

Ahmed Alignment Labs is building the quality layer for AI in Asia. We red-team, evaluate and align LLMs in the languages real users speak: Roman Urdu, Urdish, Hinglish and beyond.

We're opening contract-based, fully remote roles for people whose judgment can't be commoditized.

Who we need

⚖️ Legal & Finance Analysts (LLB, finance, banking, Shariah-compliance background)
Review model outputs for legal and financial risk, rank responses, and write step-by-step reasoning for RLHF and chain-of-thought datasets.

🩺 Medical & Pharmacy Reviewers (MBBS, Pharm-D)
Assess clinical accuracy and patient-safety risk in AI responses, and build expert-grade evaluation sets.

🗣️ Native Language Specialists (Roman Urdu, Urdu, Punjabi, Sindhi, Pashto, Hindi/Hinglish, Bengali and more)
Write and validate formal, colloquial, romanized and code-mixed test cases, including voice-note transcripts.

🛡️ Red-Team Specialists
Design adversarial prompts using slang, emotional manipulation, double meanings and legal or financial traps, and document every failure reproducibly.

🧠 ML / Software Engineers
Build evaluation pipelines and run reproducible adversarial suites (Promptfoo, Label Studio, Argilla, Python), and help develop our ethics-evaluation and benchmarking products.

📋 QA & Operations Coordinators
Allocate tasks, track inter-annotator agreement (IAA), manage deliverables across time zones, and keep every milestone on schedule.

How we work

• Remote-first, contract-based, with milestone-based payouts
• Secure environment: VPN, role-based access, signed NDA and IP assignment
• Quality gates: nothing ships without IAA review
• Work on real AI systems deployed in banking, fintech and healthcare

You'll thrive here if you

• Have deep domain or native-language expertise
• Care about precision and can explain your reasoning clearly
• Are comfortable working independently and meeting deadlines

To apply, email ahmedanalyst8001@gmail.com with:

1. Your CV or LinkedIn profile
2. The role you're applying for
3. Your domain or languages, plus a short note on why you're a fit

Please share this with someone who'd be a great fit. 🔁
